content_selection.rationale: The brief got the core stories right. Anthropic's report on Claude taking unintended actions on real websites, the White House statement that incident disclosure is "not optional", and OpenAI's misalignment report form a timely, well-supported lead cluster. The OpenAI revenue gap and Nvidia/Reflection items are also strong picks. But it dropped two widely covered stories from the same window. Satya Nadella's October 10 call to treat every AI model as compromised and fit it with an "emergency brake" was covered by TechCrunch and The Verge and speaks directly to the brief's own lead theme. A year-long Senate investigation into data-center developers (TIME exclusive, Tom's Hardware, Warren press release) also went out. Meanwhile, space went to a single headline on Cloudflare/Deno and Manus whose primary sources were never fetched. Dropping the Berkeley/CMU persistence study was right: it has been a preprint since April and got its coverage then.
content_selection.evidence: Excluded: "Nadella: assume every AI model is compromised (explainx.ai)" and "Senate investigation: data-center developers misled public on costs (explainx.ai)"; included: "Cloudflare to acquire Deno; Manus parent Butterfly Effect raises $500M+ (via AI Weekly summary; primary sources not fetched)"

selection_disagreements.story: Nadella: assume every AI model is compromised / 'emergency brake' containment essay (Oct 10)
selection_disagreements.rationale: Searching shows this was major coverage, not just an aggregator item. TechCrunch ran 'Microsoft's Satya Nadella says AI models need an emergency brake' on Oct 10, and The Verge covered the same X post. TechCrunch tied it explicitly to labs acknowledging more and more cases where they seemed to lose control of their models. It fits directly with the brief's Anthropic/White House/OpenAI incident cluster, so leaving it out drops a key industry response to the brief's main story.

selection_disagreements.story: Senate (Warren/Van Hollen/Blumenthal) investigation: data-center developers misled public on costs, jobs, NDAs
selection_disagreements.rationale: This is a substantive, well-sourced policy story: a TIME exclusive on Oct 8, Tom's Hardware on Oct 10, and an official Senate press release. It covers a year-long probe of Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, CoreWeave, Digital Realty and Equinix, with findings on roughly one permanent job per megawatt, routine NDAs, and costs shifted to ratepayers. It deserved a slot alongside the brief's infrastructure-financing coverage, and it is far stronger than an aggregator-only headline.

selection_disagreements.story: Cloudflare acquires Deno; Manus parent raises $500M+ (headline only, via AI Weekly; primaries not fetched)
selection_disagreements.rationale: The brief itself says these weren't checked against primary sources, and the Deno deal is only loosely about AI. The slot would have been better used for the Senate data-center report or Nadella's essay, both of which have strong primary and major-outlet coverage.

factual_accuracy.rationale: I checked every major section against primary sources: Anthropic's report, OpenAI's misalignment report, the arXiv abstract, Epoch's Substack summary and Bloomberg via Yahoo. I also checked strong secondary coverage from Axios, Reuters relays, TechCrunch, CBS/6abc, Retraction Watch, MarkTechPost/CellCog, Decrypt/Implicator and MacRumors. Nearly all specific figures match my research, including 722→719 manuscripts, 300 Lean formalizations (~42%), RHAE 100.0 at 44% of human actions, the $0.042 price with 83.5% vs 82.3% accuracy and 92.2 vs 93.7 calibration, $50B vs $70B, $65B, the $1.4T pre-money valuation, a 1.4% Nasdaq drop, $800M, $25B, the July 18 tip, and 19+1 visa applications. The brief also keeps the right hedges: FT/WSJ are paywalled, Microsoft's figures are its own, the arXiv results are self-reported, and the Reflection talks are early and unverified. The only issues are small: Epoch says both models padded their scores by rerunning near-identical training runs, not just Fable 5, the 'established October 4 / chaired by Jay Clayton' detail could only be partly confirmed, and the Cloudflare–Deno and Butterfly Effect item was not checked.
factual_accuracy.evidence: "In Microsoft's own 36-benchmark comparison (147,137 questions) it averages 83.5% accuracy versus 82.3% for TypeSafe's Jev 1.13.0 and 81.9% for Quyet-1.0-Large, at 85 ms median latency; on calibration it ranks third (92.2 versus Jev's 93.7)" — matches CellCog's copy of Microsoft's table exactly.

length_format.rationale: The brief has 12 Headlines bullets, inside the 8-15 target. It has 10 deep-dive items (Research 2, Industry 2, Products 2, Benchmarks 1, Policy 3), at the top of the 5-10 range but not over it, and every section is populated. Most deep-dives land at 5-6 sentences, but at least two (Microsoft-Decision-1 and the OpenAI misalignment report) run to 7 sentences. Many sentences are long, multi-clause constructions, which pushes several items past a 'dense 3-6 sentence summary' in practice and amounts to mild per-item bloat rather than a structural failure.
length_format.evidence: Microsoft-Decision-1 item runs 7 sentences, including an appended 'Separately, Liquid AI released open-weight decision models d1-3B and d1-omni-600M...' sentence. The OpenAI misalignment item adds 'A secondary writeup says the channel also disclosed two June 16–20 cases...' before its 'Why it matters' line.

dedup.rationale: Every story in today's brief that overlaps a prior edition is explicitly tagged as a follow-up and adds substantial new information. The math withdrawals, Broadcom's $50B+ financing, Nvidia–Reflection talks and the Microsoft-Decision-1 launch are all new developments, not rehashes. The other stories (Anthropic's unintended-actions report, the White House statement, the OpenAI misalignment report, Epoch InnovationEval, Memento 3, Gemini coworker agents, the Usage Policy) do not appear in the Oct 7–9 editions. Mentions of earlier items, such as Beam's October 5 launch or Anthropic's July and September incidents, serve only as background inside new stories.
